hard_gates.gate: G2 permissions: the gate catches an unchecked action planted in p00's kernel
hard_gates.evidence: Plant P3 (plants/plants.diff) is in the kernel's PermissionAuthorizationHandler (src/Kernel/Erp.Kernel/Security/Permissions.cs). It lets any signed-in caller who sends 'Authorization: Bearer' pass every permission check. A bearer token is a documented carrier: any user gets one from POST /api/auth/sign-in with issueToken:true. With CRITIC_PLANT=P3, every gate and test passed. G2 passed 36 of 36 (plant-P3.log). G1 plus the rule gates ran 99 tests (plant-P3G1.log). One failed, G1TenantSourceTests, and only on the inert text of the other plant, L4. All P3M module and kernel tests passed: Identity 100, Tenancy 33, Lists 6, Reports 53, Kernel 217. The critic's own test, CriticP3Proof.cs, proves the plant is live. With P3, the no-roles user noaccess, signed in by bearer, got 200 on GET /api/identity/users. POST /api/identity/roles got past authorization; only the module's own grant-beyond-own rule then stopped it with 403 (plant-P3PROOF.log). Without the plant, the same test passes (plant-P3NONE.log). Cause: G2's deny-by-default and grant-exactly-one tests sign in only with cookies (Env.SignInAsync). SignInWithTokenAsync is used only for administrators, in G1 and in one identity test.

hard_gates.gate: G1 tenant isolation: the gate catches a leak planted in p00's kernel
hard_gates.evidence: Plant L4 adds a 'fast total' in kernel ListBinding.QueryAsync. It keeps a list query's total for 120 s in AppContext data, keyed by row type, search and filter, with no tenant. It was caught twice. Statically, G1TenantSourceTests reported 'ListBinding.cs:272 keeps state in a process-wide store outside fields (AppContext…)'. Live, G1HttpIsolationTests reported 'GET /api/identity/users?search=bravocnry… 200 total 1 but for a value that exists nowhere total 0' (plant-L4.log, 60 G1 tests, 34 min).

hard_gates.gate: G1 tenant isolation: critic's live attack (API, documented query parameters, bearer, exports, files, side channels, DB role)
hard_gates.evidence: attack/attack.mjs reuses the r8 critic's script, extended. It ran as the alnoor admin (A) against gulfsteel (B), after B made a canary user, 10 saved views (private and shared), a company logo, 5 roles and 5 users. A sent: 109 operations with B's ids in path, query and body; 686 requests that set every documented query parameter (uuid ones to each of B's company, branch, role, user and tenant ids; groupBy and columns to tenant fields), each by cookie and by A's own Bearer token; 465 tenant-switch header, query and cookie requests; 100 export requests (csv, xlsx, pdf, json, html in en and ar, with company=B); 35 filter-language and cursor requests. Results: LEAKS 0. No answer carried any of 217 B-only ids. A superuser md5 of B's rows in all 17 tenant tables was identical before and after (b-before-attack.txt, b-after-attack.txt). A's list totals did not move when B wrote. Row versions look random. db-roles-rls.txt: erp_app is NOSUPERUSER, NOBYPASSRLS and NOINHERIT, owns nothing and belongs to no role. All 17 tenant tables have tenant_id NOT NULL with RLS enabled, forced and with policies. As erp_app bound to A: B rows visible 0, an UPDATE of B touched 0, an INSERT for B was refused by RLS. With no tenant bound, or with a session-level setting and no transaction marker, 0 rows are visible. pg_stat_user_tables gives permission denied. identity.sign_in_secret has no erp_app grant. Exactly 2 SECURITY DEFINER functions exist (resolve_session, verify_sign_in). No jobs exist yet (p12).

biggest_gap.title: The permission gate (G2) checks only cookie sessions, so a kernel fault that lets any Bearer-token caller skip every permission check passes all 1,501 tests
biggest_gap.detail: Signing in with issueToken:true gives any user a Bearer token, and the API accepts it on every endpoint. G2's deny-by-default test ('a user whose roles grant nothing is denied everything') and its 'granting exactly one permission opens exactly the endpoints that declare it' test sign in only through Env.SignInAsync, which is cookie-based. Bearer sessions appear only for administrators, in G1 and in one identity test, and an administrator holds every permission anyway. A plant in the kernel's PermissionAuthorizationHandler lets any Bearer caller pass every requirement. With it, a no-roles user reads all 100,000 users and reaches every write's own business checks. G1, G2, the rule gates and every module and kernel test still pass. For a UAE company that connects an integration (e-commerce, a POS or a bank feed) through the API, this is the most likely path to over-privilege, and nothing would detect it. Fix: run both G2 matrices (no roles denied everything; exactly one permission opens exactly its endpoints) once per credential carrier: cookie, Bearer, and any carrier added later. Make the carrier list come from SessionAuthenticationHandler.ReadToken, or a reviewed list, so a new carrier cannot be left out. Add a self-test that plants this bypass and must fail.
biggest_gap.evidence: plants/plants.diff, P3 hunk in src/Kernel/Erp.Kernel/Security/Permissions.cs, active only when CRITIC_PLANT=P3. Run plants/run-plants.sh in the toolbox (erp-toolbox:pw1.63.0-net10, mounted as in ./erp run_toolbox) with PLANTS='P3 P3G1 P3M P3PROOF P3NONE'. Results: plant-P3.log, G2 36 of 36 passed; plant-P3G1.log, G1 and Rules 99 tests, whose only failure is the inert text of plant L4; plant-P3M-*.log, 409 module and kernel tests all passed; plant-P3PROOF.log, CriticP3Proof.cs failed with 'no-roles user with a bearer token: GET /api/identity/users -> 200, POST /api/identity/roles -> 403 identity.grantBeyondOwn'; plant-P3NONE.log, the same test passes without the plant. Source: tests/Erp.Gates.Tests/G2/G2PermissionTests.cs lines 324-389 use Env.SignInAsync only, and grep finds no SignInWithTokenAsync in tests/Erp.Gates.Tests/G2.

other_findings: Processor time: verify used 10,313 s against the owner's 10,500 s maximum, a 1.8% margin, with load up to 95 on 16 CPUs; dotnet alone used 8,214 s. Round 8's two runs used 11,671 s (busy) and 8,694 s (quiet), so this round's processor time cut kept a busy run under the maximum, but only just. Wall time was 5,016 s and was not judged (busy machine).

Kernel Money disagrees with the signed-off rule docs/compliance/vat-rounding-and-currency.md, rule 2 ('Lines and tax-category subtotals keep their full precision; the invoice total is rounded'). (a) Money.Create refuses any amount with more decimals than the currency's minor units, so a line cannot keep full precision. (b) Money.Create rounds every base amount to the fils, and Money.Add sums those rounded base amounts. Example: three lines of USD 1.00 at 3.6725 add up to a base of 11.01 AED, while converting the 3.00 USD total once gives 11.02. The MinorUnits table is also written from memory, not from docs/compliance (src/Kernel/Erp.Kernel/Money/Money.cs lines 24-29 and 90-96, 104-109). Nothing uses Money yet, so this can be fixed before p08 builds on it.

Keyboard (round 7 and round 8 finding, still open): in the shell, Tab after 'My account' lands on the document body before 'Skip to content', a dead stop each cycle (browser-notes.txt: 'BODY stops in Tab cycle: 2' in 40 presses).

[route: p03-identity] Sign-in lockout (round 7 and round 8 finding, still open): after 8 failures, the right password still gets only 'Sign-in failed. Check your e-mail and password and try again.', with no hint that the account is paused or for how long (browser-notes.txt, attack/empty.mjs).

[route: p01-odoo-rig] In 1 of 3 Odoo sign-in runs, the Odoo driver's 'returning' variant timed out in set-up: it waited 120 s for input[name=login], but Odoo opened /odoo/contacts because the set-up session was still alive (compare/results/sign-in-20261011T053027-a977.json). Because of that one errored run, run.mjs exited 1.

pg_class.reltuples stays readable to erp_app: it gives 101,010 for identity.users, a figure that counts every tenant. Only the new static ban (Product_code_never_reads_statistics…) guards it, and a regex can be evaded, for example by building the column name at run time. The r8 hardening of the pg_stat views is in place and verified (permission denied for pg_stat_user_tables).

Round 8's shared-device gap is fixed: with erp.passkeyOffer=1, typing in the e-mail field withdraws the passkey request, and e-mail, Enter, password, Enter signs in (attack/shared-device.txt). After a password sign-in the device stops asking on arrival (value '2'). The remembered-domain feature stores only salted hashes of domains, and it moves on only for domains this device signed in to: another workspace's address does not move on.

The device keeps erp.lastEmail in localStorage after a session that ended without the Sign out button. That is acceptable for 'returning', but on a shared PC the next person sees the previous person's e-mail unless the Sign out button was used.

Plant L4 (a cross-tenant list-total cache in AppContext data inside kernel ListBinding) was caught both statically (G1TenantSourceTests) and live (G1HttpIsolationTests: a search for B's canary answered total 1 against total 0 for a value that exists nowhere).

OpenAPI at /api/openapi/v1.json lists 112 operations, the same as round 8. English and Arabic: the sign-in and shell switch to rtl/ar. In the Arabic shell, the only Latin text is company codes, 'Ctrl', the 'English' switch and the workspace code. An empty workspace provisioned in Arabic signs in by keyboard in 0.87 s to an RTL home. The no-roles user sees 'No areas are open to you yet' and gets 403 from the API.
